violated_constraint.engine_rule: Temporal: 'Workflow code must be deterministic to support replay' and 'put [LLM/AI invocations] in Activities' so a re-executed Workflow Function issues the same sequence of Commands. Restate: non-deterministic operations must be wrapped (ctx.run) to ensure deterministic replay; replay skips executing journaled actions and uses the recorded result; the SDK schedules the run closure only if the run wasn't replayed. DBOS: a workflow function must invoke the same steps with the same inputs in the same order given recorded step return values; third-party API calls must not run directly in the workflow function.
violated_constraint.name: command-sequence (journal-entry / step-sequence) identity of the orchestration function under replay
violated_constraint.property_llm_breaks: An LLM call is not a function of recorded history: sampling and HTTP I/O can yield a different token sequence, hence a different subsequent command/journal/step sequence, when the orchestration function is re-executed. That is the determinism property Temporal, Restate and DBOS require of the replayed function.

answer.why_not_partial: Calling replay 'partially possible' names no property. Engines do not replay a fraction of an LLM sample. They exclude the LLM invocation from the replayed function by wrapping it, then require the remaining orchestration to be fully command-sequence-identical given the recorded bytes. The LLM step therefore satisfies durability-of-recorded-result and does not satisfy orchestration-function determinism.

claims.strongest_caveat: Captured docs are HTML/markdown bytes at fetch_timestamp; vendor pages can change. GitHub contents JSON is a structured API rail pinned to a commit SHA. claims.claim: The specific determinism property an LLM step breaks is command-sequence (or journal-entry / step-sequence) identity of the orchestration function under replay. LLM sampling and HTTP I/O are not functions of recorded history; re-executing them inside the replayed function can emit a different command/journal/step sequence. Wrapping the call as an Activity, ctx.run, or @DBOS.step does not make the model deterministic — it moves the non-determinism off the replay path so the recorded bytes can be reused. Replay of an LLM workflow is therefore not 'partially possible': the LLM invocation is excluded from the replayed function, and the remaining orchestration is fully constrained to recorded results.

claims.claim: The subset that CAN be replayed deterministically is: (1) pure control-flow in the orchestration function that branches only on values already recorded in history/journal/checkpoints; (2) SDK-wrapped time, timers, and UUIDs whose results are journaled; (3) versioning/patch markers that select a recorded code path; (4) the scheduling of side-effect wrappers, not their live re-execution. Explicitly excluded: LLM token sampling, raw HTTP, unrecorded wall-clock, unrecorded PRNG, and process-local mutable globals.
